supersedes: engineering 8.0 / customer-ready 6.8, graded 2026-08-23 against the integrate/monday-pilot build
how_this_was_graded: Customer-ready was re-graded by WALKING the product in a real browser, not by counting closed blockers. Thirty staff-facing screens were opened as a signed-in super admin against a LOCAL PRODUCTION BUILD (npm run build, then npm run start) via e2e/screen-walk.spec.ts, which records each screen's rendered text, load time, console errors, page errors and failed requests to e2e/.artifacts/screen-walk/*.json. The grade below is read off those artefacts. Where a dimension cannot be seen from a browser (personal data leaving to a third party, absence of a privacy policy) the evidence is a named file, and it says so.

engineering.band_position: inside the Tier P target band (8.5-9.5), at its floor
engineering.verdict: Real, tested, production software. Two of the three gaps that held this at 8.0 are now closed with named evidence; one remains and it cannot be checked from here.

evidence_run_today.typecheck: npm run typecheck -> tsc --noEmit, 0 errors, strict

evidence_run_today.build: npm run build -> exit 0, webpack production build, TypeScript check passed

COVERAGE THRESHOLDS ARE ENFORCED - VERIFIED TODAY, and this closes an item that had been recorded as unproven since 2026-08-09. vitest.config.ts sets real thresholds (lines 56, functions 76, branches 78, statements 56) ratcheted to just under measured reality, and .github/workflows/ci.yml:45 runs `npm run test:coverage` in the merge-blocking verify job - so a drop below them fails the build rather than being reported and ignored.

This is the ONLY remaining gap between this grade and a 9, and it needs one look at a dashboard that was in a partial outage on 2026-08-27.
engineering.why_not_higher: The standard requires every gate present AND passing, verified by running it. Observed error-monitoring arrival is not verified, so 9 would be a false 9.
engineering.why_not_lower: Two gaps closed since the 8.0 with named, re-runnable evidence: J5 end-to-end coverage (cycle 43) and enforced coverage thresholds (verified today in both the config and the CI step). A grade is a claim about evidence, and the evidence moved.
engineering.why_this_is_not_grade_inflation: The 8.0 was recorded with THREE unproven items and an explicit note that rounding to 8.5 to reach the tier band would be a false 9. Two of those three are now closed by artefacts a reader can go and run. The third is named above rather than absorbed.

customer_ready.cap_note: Each cap was checked against the walk. No broken core journey (all 30 screens render and navigate; the core job is covered end to end by a merge-blocking test AND was performed for real once on 2026-08-26). No cross-customer leakage (BC-01 green and proven capable of catching one; E-06 fixed in cycle 42). No placeholder content. Deployment, health check and monitoring all present. The dev-ism cap was CONSIDERED and deliberately NOT applied - see blocker CR-08 for the reasoning, which is recorded rather than buried.

scorecard.observed: The core job is now proven twice over: a real email genuinely left the system on 2026-08-26 at 12:16:36 UTC through the real queue worker with its raw MIME inspected (docs/ops/SEND-PROOF-2026-08-26.md), and the full enrol-launch-send-reply-opt-out chain is covered by a merge-blocking integration test proven capable of failing. Was 5, graded down then for the unknown. Not 9 or 10: the browser walk is navigation-only, so no human has clicked compose-send-reply through the UI on this build.

All 30 screens render real content with a real heading - no stubs, no 'coming soon', no placeholder text, no error-boundary strings, and zero failed requests across the whole walk. Held at 8 because two DESIGN.json signature elements (the send rail, live/dry banding) are specified and NOT built - absent rather than half-built, so a customer does not hit them.

A pattern scan across all 30 rendered screens for raw enums, env-var names, cuids, stack traces and ISO timestamps returned exactly ONE hit - a raw correlation cuid on the outbound email detail page (CR-08). Everything else is clean. Down from 9 because the previous 13-page pass never opened that screen.

Coherent and structured across the walk, real empty states, no layout breakage, zero console noise. The design system is now ENFORCED by 55 tests that compute WCAG 2.2 AA contrast properly and already caught five genuine live accessibility failures. Held at 8: three measured contrast defects remain open in DESIGN.json, and mobile/responsive was again not checked.

Up from 6. The contradiction that cost it those points is GONE - verified on this walk, not inferred: the client Overview's numbered workflow no longer makes an Activity claim at all. The copy is genuinely careful about what it does and does not promise: 'Sent from mailbox means ODoutreach handed the email to the connected mailbox/provider. It does not guarantee inbox placement', and Delivered reads '-' with 'Outlook and Gmail do not report this back'.

The client Overview walks a numbered 1-8 setup workflow with per-step status and a '2 / 8 complete' counter, each step explaining in plain English what to do and why. Empty workspaces give real empty states that name the next action.

Up from 6. Off-happy-path is now actually tested rather than assumed: a failed brief save shows an inline error and KEEPS the operator's typed data instead of crashing (brief-save-session-expiry.spec.ts); an unknown id renders the 404 UI and discloses nothing; unauthenticated access redirects to sign-in with a callback. Zero console and page errors across 30 screens. Still unchecked: network failure mid-journey, form validation beyond the brief save, mobile.

DOWN from 7, and this is the finding of this pass. Isolation genuinely improved - E-06 is fixed, BC-01 is green and proven capable of catching a leak, and the hard rule is visible in production as allowlistedClients:1. But prospect personal data is leaving the building right now: sentry.server.config.ts and sentry.edge.config.ts still have userInfo and httpBodies commented out, so names, email addresses and the bodies of real outreach and real replies are collected into error reports sent to a third party whose Art.28 DPA is not yet accepted (CR-06).

Up from 5. /api/health returns ok with database ok; monitoring cannot be off by a missing setting; docs/TEAM_RUNBOOK.md exists; CI is merge-blocking and deploys are verified by hash. The bounce rate finally has a real writer (record-bounce.ts) - but it has never been seen firing in production, because nothing has sent since 3 July (CR-01b).

DOWN from 6. Workspace creation, staff invite and access toggling, soft-delete with recovery and a working support-ticket form are all present and were walked. But there is NO terms of service and NO privacy policy anywhere in src/app - checked by search, not assumed - and this product processes third-party personal data under UK GDPR and PECR (CR-07).

customer_ready.movement_from_6_8: Net +0.58. Up: core journeys 5->8 (+54), copy 6->8 (+16), operability 5->7 (+12), error handling 6->7 (+10). Down: dev-isms 9->7 (-20), data safety 7->6 (-10), commercial 6->5 (-4). The rise is real but it is NOT the whole story - two dimensions fell, and both fell on findings this pass made rather than inherited.
customer_ready.limitation: This walked a FIXTURE database of four near-empty workspaces on a LOCAL production build, not the live site with seventeen real clients. It is strong evidence about rendering, copy, empty states, leakage and error paths, and weak evidence about data scale. Load times (1.3-5.9s) are local numbers under eight parallel workers hitting a cold server and are a floor for production, not a prediction of it. Two long-standing data-scale questions remain neither confirmed nor refuted.

blockers.summary: Prospect personal data and email bodies are being sent to Sentry right now. sentry.server.config.ts and sentry.edge.config.ts are unchanged installer scaffolding with userInfo:false and httpBodies:[] left COMMENTED OUT, so the SDK defaults apply and collect user info and HTTP request bodies - on this product that is prospect names, addresses and the text of real outreach and real replies. The DSN is hard-coded so this cannot be off. tracesSampleRate is 1, sampling 100%. The fix is to uncomment two lines in two files and choose a real trace rate; it removes the personal data from error monitoring without removing the monitoring.

There is no terms of service and no privacy policy anywhere in the product. Searched src/app for privacy, terms and legal routes: none exist. For a product processing third-party personal data under UK GDPR and PECR this is a genuine commercial-mechanics gap, and it is also the document a client asks for when they ask who else sees their prospects' data.

A raw correlation cuid is shown ungated on the outbound email detail page (src/app/(app)/activity/outbound/[id]/page.tsx:66-67, a Routing card described as 'Workspace-scoped identifiers for provider correlation'). This is NOT super-admin gated - journeys.spec.ts:95 explicitly asserts that non-super-admin staff can open that page. The 6.0 dev-ism cap was considered and deliberately NOT applied: the scan found this one leak across 30 screens, it sits on a card whose stated purpose is diagnostics, and the page's only index (/activity) is itself super-admin gated - so an ordinary operator reaches it only by direct link. Recording the decision rather than burying it, so the next grader can disagree.

The bounce rate has never been OBSERVED firing in production. The structural defect is fixed - both channels now write the BOUNCED status through src/server/email/outbound/record-bounce.ts - but nothing has sent since 3 July, so no real NDR has arrived to move the number off zero. Until it does, the reported bounce rate is a fix that has not fired, which is this project's most repeated defect class. Separately unresolved: whether a bounce rate with no data behind it should render as 0% at all rather than 'no data yet'. A confident wrong number is worse than a blank.
Mobile and responsive layout has never been checked, on this pass or either previous one. It is recorded as unproven rather than assumed fine.

Art.28 data-processing agreements. Researched 2026-08-27 from each vendor's published DPA: RESEND binds automatically via its Terms of Service, including EU and UK SCCs (resend.com/legal/dpa) - nothing to do. ROCKETREACH forms part of its Terms of Service with no separate signature (rocketreach.co/dpa), though note the role split - it is an INDEPENDENT CONTROLLER for the prospect records it sells and a processor only for data we supply. SENTRY is the one real action and it is self-serve: Greg accepts it under Legal & Compliance in the Sentry org settings. Attempted 2026-08-27 at approximately 10:00 UTC and blocked by a Sentry platform outage, not by inaction. Record the who-and-when Sentry's page shows afterwards, not a bare assertion.

The bounce rate was structurally pinned at 0%: the metric counted OutboundEmail.status BOUNCED, which only the Resend webhook ever wrote, while all outreach goes out through Microsoft Graph or Gmail. Both channels now write through one function.

sell_gate.note: PROVE DOES NOT CLOSE. The instruction was to re-grade and record, and closing PROVE was conditional on both grades reaching 8. Customer-ready reached 7.4. Closing every named blocker was necessary for an 8 and was not sufficient - the walk found three things nobody had recorded before (CR-06, CR-07, CR-08), which is exactly what walking is for and exactly what counting closed rows would have missed. The distance to 8 is 0.6 and it is cheap: CR-06 is two commented-out lines in two files, CR-07 is two documents, CR-08 is one gated field. Together those three would move dimensions 8, 10 and 3 and land customer-ready at roughly 8.1.

questions_for_greg: Accept the Sentry Art.28 DPA when Sentry is back up (CR-05) - it is one self-serve acceptance under Legal & Compliance and it is the only DPA that needs an action.

Whose words go in the terms of service and privacy policy (CR-07)? The pages can be built, but what they promise a client about data retention and sub-processors is a commercial commitment, not an engineering one.
